# cwd doesn't work

Fix the `cwd` alias (copy the current directory to the clipboard):

```bash
$ cwd
tr: illegal option -- \
usage: tr [-Ccsu] string1 string2
       tr [-Ccu] -d string1
       tr [-Ccu] -s string1 string2
       tr [-Ccu] -ds string1 string2
```

The alias piped `pwd` through `tr -d '\n'`; inside the single-quoted alias body the inner quoting was wrong, so `tr` received `\n` as an option (or the backslash alone) instead of the string to delete, and nothing reached `pbcopy`.

Expected: `cwd` puts the current path, without a trailing newline, on the clipboard.
